description: The Drone Swarm Search Environment is a Python simulation package from the Insper DSSE project for developing maritime search-and-rescue policies. It provides one environment in which shipwreck survivors drift within a probability grid and another that uses OpenDrift particle simulations with ocean and wind forcing. Multiple drone agents search for people or cover high-probability areas, allowing researchers to train and compare reinforcement-learning policies. Spatial domains, grid resolution and episode duration are configured by the user, not tied to a fixed coast or observation period. The public repository provides examples, tests, documentation and installation through PyPI. Source code is free under MIT. This supports emergency-response planning and investigation of drone search coverage. A limitation is that success in a simulated probability field does not establish field reliability, survivor detection accuracy or operational approval. OpenDrift is an optional physical-drift dependency; no directly related existing catalogue record was established for DSSE. This review did not install the package or run rescue simulations.
